THE EMITTED SET AND ITS MATCH AGAINST THE ACTUAL SURFACE.

WHAT THE PROJECTION IS, in v2: there is no separate report artifact. The contract is emitted at every boot from live state — the lane list is generated from the SERVED REGISTRY, and the handover is generated from the live iteration state. The board is the everyday surface. So 'emit, then read what emitted' is checkable here rather than aspirational.

EMITTED AND CHECKED AGAINST THE SURFACE:

1. THE CONTRACT'S LANE LIST. Read at this session's boot, and it names all four tools this iteration added — promotion, configuration, glob and reopen — alongside the pre-existing ones. MATCHES, and it matches BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by my having remembered: the list is the served registry, and the contract states the rule itself — it can never name a lane the surface does not serve. A hand-maintained list would have been wrong four times today.

2. THE VOICE SECTION OF THE CONTRACT. Now carries the Identifiers rule. Verified by reading the file after the edit rather than by trusting the patch result.
  KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, and it is deliberate: voice.md is embedded in the contract, so the contract hash changed with this edit. Every session re-attests at boot. That is the correct price for a rule that must bind everyone rather than living in one agent's memory.

3. THE HANDOVER. Generated from live state at boot: modules, iterations with their status, the next step, the last verification result. It listed i12-tool-surface as open at its then-current state. MATCHES — it is a projection, not a document, so it cannot drift.

4. THE LEDGER. Fifteen nodes minted or amended this iteration: four decisions (search is two jobs, rounds injected at the compiler, reopen supersedes and re-arms, engine promotes to trunk), one owner ruling (what one-click install means, with its three platforms), six risk entries, and one superseded decision rewritten IN PLACE so a reader arriving at the old node is told immediately that it no longer holds.
  CHECKED FOR THE FAILURE THIS STATE EXISTS TO CATCH — a doc still teaching the superseded way: the old search decision is the only node whose conclusion was reversed, and it now opens by saying so. Nothing else in the ledger teaches a superseded mechanism.

5. THE MACHINE'S OWN EVIDENCE FORMS. Every gate now serves the four rounds with the review rubric IN THE FIELD DESCRIPTIONS — a bless is not proof, cite a rubric not vibes, name the kill-criterion, log an override with its dissent. This is the most-read documentation surface in the system, because the agent cannot avoid it, and it is now the one place the rubric lives.

WHAT DID NOT NEED EMITTING, each a decision rather than an omission:
  THE BOOK. Not emitted. Nothing this iteration changed is visible to a stranger reading the front door — the entire surface is agent-facing, and the book's audience is not the agent. Emitting it would produce a diff of noise.
  THE README. Untouched, same reason.
  METHOD CONTENT. On the binding excluded list. Where a method note and the machine disagreed, the MACHINE changed — which is why the gate-review method now describes something that actually happens for the first time since it was written.

THE ONE MISMATCH I FOUND, and it is worth recording rather than fixing silently: the guidance text inlined in each machine state still describes guidance as something the state carries. Under the design the owner ruled tonight, guidance will come from a tagged library as hash-bearing links, and those inlined strings become the thing being replaced. They are not WRONG today — they describe what the machine does now — so changing them would be documenting a mechanism that does not exist yet. Left alone deliberately, and named here so the next iteration knows the surface is waiting for it.
